title: Complete a café visit
explanation:
A short café visit strings together everything in this skill. Greet first: in the morning, *buenos días* [1]. If you introduce yourself, use *me llamo* [2].

Order with the right article (café is masculine, *un café* [3]) and soften with the conditional, which makes a request more polite [4]. Ask the server things with *usted* and third-person verbs if you don't know them [5]. Read prices in euros and céntimos [6].

Plan before you speak. List your turns (greet, order, ask, close), choose formal or familiar once, and keep it consistent through the whole conversation.
keyIdeas: Choose usted or tú once and stay consistent.
Soften requests with the conditional and por favor.

workedExample.problem: You have already greeted the server, a stranger. Script your next three turns: say that you are Marta, order a black coffee politely, and ask the server's name.
steps: Introduce yourself with llamarse in the first person: Me llamo Marta.
Order with un + masculine café and the polite conditional of querer: Querría un café negro, por favor.
Stranger, so ask with usted and the third-person form: ¿Cómo se llama usted?
Check consistency: every turn stays formal, with no tú forms.
workedExample.answer: Me llamo Marta. Querría un café negro, por favor. ¿Cómo se llama usted?

pitfalls: Switching between tú and usted in the same conversation.
Forgetting article agreement (un café) under time pressure.
Skipping the greeting and opening with a bare order.

citations.quote: La fórmula de saludo que se emplea durante la mañana es, en el español general, buenos días.
Tener el nombre o la denominación que se expresa.
Como determinante, toma la forma un ante sustantivos masculinos, los preceda inmediatamente o no
Courtesy: Using this mood softens a request, making it more polite.
formal singular; used when addressing a person respectfully, someone older, someone not known to the speaker, or someone of some social distance
